A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SKETCH research work. All 16 pages, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–F, support reliable comparison through text extraction and rendered-page inspection.

before.justification: v3 reports original AIS trajectory and NKP prediction experiments, including quantitative comparisons, ablations, horizon analyses and qualitative examples in Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including the quantitative results in Tables 2–5 and 7 and the qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: The NKP-conditioned architecture, retrieval-based intent prediction, contrastive objective, staged training, inference procedure and coordinate updates are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same private container-vessel AIS data and public cargo-vessel evaluation, with unchanged prediction horizons and open-set NKP scenarios.

E2.justification: MP-LSTM, TrAISformer, DiffuTraj and AISFuser remain in the same trajectory comparisons. Random Forest and the same NKP model variants remain in the NKP comparisons.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, MMSI-based splits, five-minute resampling, sample counts, model configurations and training settings are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices E–F.

E4.justification: The NKP-quality and channel ablations, public-data generalization test, horizon analysis and qualitative cases are retained. Removing plot titles does not change the analyses or examples.

E5.justification: The same-random-seed statement for the qualitative ablation and statistical reporting practices are unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals or significance tests for model performance.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted trajectories match. For example, Table 2 retains the proposed model's MSEP of 4.40e-5 and MFD of 0.63; the changed qualitative images differ only in their title regions.

T1.justification: The NKP definition, mathematical formulation, assumptions and coordinate equations are identical, as are the proofs and derivations in Appendices A, C and D.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about hierarchical intent conditioning, open-set NKP inference and long-horizon prediction performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of conditioning, numerical stability, generalization and NKP-related failure modes are unchanged. No applicability boundary or limitation is added or revised.

D1.justification: v4 removes the MMSI identifiers and start indices contained in the subplot titles of Tables 1 and 8, losing details identifying the displayed vessel trajectory windows. Implementation, preprocessing, hardware and code/data-access disclosures otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list and positioning relative to earlier trajectory prediction, retrieval and contrastive-learning research are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v3 dated 29 May 2026 to v4 dated 21 July 2026. The paper's prose, terminology, section ordering and appendix structure are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: v4 removes the per-panel trajectory-comparison titles from the four plots in Table 1 and eight plots in Appendix B's Table 8. Their curves, axes, legends, captions and placement are retained; other displays are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Removing the small subplot titles in Tables 1 and 8 reduces visual clutter but also removes vessel/window identifiers. This limited presentation and traceability tradeoff does not meaningfully alter overall quality: the methods, experimental evidence, theory and explanatory text remain unchanged.
